Definition: Zimri, the name of five Israelites, and of an Arabian tribe
BiblicalUsage: Zimri is a name worn by very different men. One is the Simeonite prince slain by Phinehas at Peor; another is the commander who murdered King Elah and reigned seven days before burning the palace over his own head; a third is a son of Zerah in Judah's line. Their full stories live on their People profiles.
TheologicalSignificance: I believe the two famous Zimris are a matched warning: one died for open sin in the camp, the other for treason on the throne. The same name, the same end — sin does not care how high the seat is.
RelatedPeople: Zimri, Son of Salu; Zimri, King of Israel; Zimri, Son of Jehoadah
RelatedEvents: Israel's Sin at Peor and Phinehas
